decisions.quote:
Thus, one central point of this endeavor was to examine whether or not we could (conceptually or directly) replicate Cannon
and Woodward (2012) and contribute thus to the theoretical debate by examining the robustness of a key finding.
decisions.location: 1. Introduction, p. 3, lines 193-194 (reference entry at References, p. 20, lines 1194-1195)
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly re-tests Cannon and Woodward (2012) across Study 1 (Experiments 1-5) and Study 2. Shipped row 1044 refers to this same study ('Infants generate goal‐based action predictions' by Cannon & Woodward) but lists an erroneous DOI (10.1111/j.1467-7687.2011.01127.x) and year (2011). The primary text's reference list (p. 20, lines 1194-1195) confirms the blind coding's target 0 metadata: Cannon, E., & Woodward, A. L. (2012), 'Infants generate goal-based action predictions.', Developmental Science, 15, 292-298, DOI 10.1111/j.1467-7687.2011.01095.x.

decisions.quote:
However, despite our systematic variation of any other factors that could have had an influence on infants’ action perception
(such as type of agent, presence of an occluder or number of learning- and test trials), we failed to replicate the findings of Cannon
and Woodward (2012) across all our experiments and labs.
decisions.reason: With the dependent original identity resolved to Cannon and Woodward (2012), the authors state an explicit overall replication verdict that they failed to replicate the findings of Cannon and Woodward (2012) across all experiments and both laboratories (also stated in the Abstract, lines 50-51). Both shipped and blind correctly code the outcome as 'failed'.

decisions.quote:
Two different labs collaborated over the attempt to replicate both conceptually and directly the findings reported by
Cannon and Woodward (2012).
decisions.reason: The paper collects new eye-tracking data from independent participant samples across two laboratories (Study 1: N = 144 across 5 experiments; Study 2: N = 104) to conceptually and directly re-test the published findings of Cannon and Woodward (2012). Both shipped and blind correctly classify the record type as 'replication'.

corrected_value.authors: Daum, M. M., Attig, M., Gunawan, R., Prinz, W., & Gredebäck, G.
corrected_value.title: Actions seen through babies’ eyes: A dissociation between looking time and predictive gaze.

decisions.quote:
Considering the path-paradigm with the animated agent, 11-month-olds looked longer towards the familiarized
path leading to the novel goal. Hence results are similar to Study 1 and Daum et al. (2012).
decisions.reason: Across Study 1 (Experiment 1, which directly uses the animated fish stimuli from Daum et al., 2012 with an occluder, and the direct replication experiment in Section 2.5) and Study 2 (path-paradigm with 11-month-olds, 32-month-olds, and adults), the paper empirically re-tests Daum et al.'s (2012) finding that infants and toddlers anticipate the old movement path (novel goal) for an occluded non-human animated agent whereas adults anticipate the familiarized goal. The authors explicitly formulate hypotheses from Daum et al. (2012) and compare their new empirical results to Daum et al. (2012) in both Study 1 and Study 2 discussions. The only shipped row for this work (row 1044) is Cannon and Woodward (2011/2012, DOI 10.1111/j.1467-7687.2011.01127.x), which is a different original study by different authors.

corrected_value.authors: Pfundmair, M., Zwarg, C., Paulus, M., & Rimpel, A.
corrected_value.title: Oxytocin promotes attention to social cues regardless of group membership.

decisions.quote:
Pfundmair et al. (2017) found that adults anticipated the goal of a grasping hand as well as of a grasping claw, which is in contrast to
our findings.
decisions.reason: In Study 2, the authors administer the Cannon and Woodward hand-paradigm to an adult sample to re-test Pfundmair et al.'s (2017) empirical finding that adults tested on the Cannon and Woodward paradigm anticipate the familiarized goal of a grasping hand. In Section 3, they hypothesize adult goal anticipations based on Pfundmair et al. (2017), and in Section 3.3 they explicitly note that Pfundmair et al. (2017) is the only prior study to test the Cannon and Woodward paradigm in adults and contrast Pfundmair et al.'s goal-anticipation result with their own adult hand-paradigm finding of path/trajectory anticipation. The only shipped row (row 1044) is Cannon and Woodward (2011/2012), which tested 11-month-old infants and is a distinct original work.
